Definition: from a derivative of G1097; to make known; subjectively, to know:--certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot.
BiblicalUsage: The word gnōrízō carries the sense of certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot. In Luke 2:15, the text says "which the Lord hath made known unto us." In John 15:15, the text says "for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, gnōrízō is a reminder that the gospel was never meant to stay where it started — it goes out, because God sends it out. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Pentecost; The Birth of Jesus; The Vine and the Branches
